summary: This is a bash script that sets up strict error handling, defines a chain of functions that call each other in sequence, initializes a logging module, and then runs the main function which prints welcome messages and executes the function chain. It's structured to be modular and use logging throughout.

explanations.2: These options make bash exit immediately if any command fails (errexit) and treat undefined variables as errors (nounset), making the script more robust.
explanations.37: This loads another script file called log.sh into the current shell so we can use the log::write function defined in it.
explanations.44: $* expands to all the arguments passed to the script, so this logs whatever parameters were given when running the script.
explanations.54: This calls the __main function and passes all command-line arguments to it using "$@" (which preserves spacing better than $*).
